name: Nineties Church — Pre-Collapse Retro Devotion
description: Nineties Church members are obsessed with the 1990s CE — not as history but as mythology, a lost paradise of perceived simplicity, bright plastic, early internet innocence, and a world before the Cascade years. They collect physical media (CDs, VHS cassettes, cartridge games), wear reconstructed fashion, and gather in 'parishes' — living rooms and back rooms decorated in meticulous period recreation. Unlike Twenty-Twentiers who romanticize collapse, Nineties Church is pre-lapsarian: they want the world just before everything went wrong. Their liturgical text is a hand-copied zine called 'Before the Flood' compiled by founder Jessamyn Petrov-Oduya, now in its 34th edition.
cultural_impact: Nineties Church has driven a significant collector economy in physical media salvage, and their aesthetic has been partially absorbed into mainstream Tier 3 interior design — 'lo-fi warm' is now a licensed NestCorp home style. Authentic period objects command prices wildly disproportionate to their function.
locations: Our Lady of the Dial-Up (basement parish, Wicker Park remnant)
The 90s Flea, monthly Ghost Market, the Gray Zone adjacent
story_hooks: A cache of genuinely original 1990s media is discovered in a sealed building during demolition — every Nineties Church parish wants it, and the bidding turns ugly.
Someone is producing high-quality fakes of period objects and selling them into the collector market; a devotee who built their identity on a fake must decide whether to expose the forger.
A corporate heritage brand wants to license Nineties Church aesthetics for a product line — the community fractures between those who see it as validation and those who see it as desecration.
